ESV.1: I came to my garden, my sister, my bride, I gathered my myrrh with my spice, I ate my honeycomb with my honey, I drank my wine with my milk. Others Eat, friends, drink, and be drunk with love!
ESV.2: I slept, but my heart was awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking. “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is wet with dew, my locks with the drops of the night.”
ESV.3: I had put off my garment; how could I put it on? I had bathed my feet; how could I soil them?
ESV.4: My beloved put his hand to the latch, and my heart was thrilled within me.
ESV.5: I arose to open to my beloved, and my hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the bolt.
ESV.6: I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had turned and gone. My soul failed me when he spoke. I sought him, but found him not; I called him, but he gave no answer.
ESV.7: The watchmen found me as they went about in the city; they beat me, they bruised me, they took away my veil, those watchmen of the walls.
ESV.8: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him I am sick with love.
ESV.9: What is your beloved more than another beloved, O most beautiful among women? What is your beloved more than another beloved, that you thus adjure us?
ESV.10: My beloved is radiant and ruddy, distinguished among ten thousand.
ESV.11: His head is the finest gold; his locks are wavy, black as a raven.
ESV.12: His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, bathed in milk, sitting beside a full pool.
ESV.13: His cheeks are like beds of spices, mounds of sweet-smelling herbs. His lips are lilies, dripping liquid myrrh.
ESV.14: His arms are rods of gold, set with jewels. His body is polished ivory,  bedecked with sapphires.
ESV.15: His legs are alabaster columns, set on bases of gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.
ESV.16: His mouth  is most sweet, and he is altogether desirable. This is my beloved and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

NKJV.1: I have come to my garden, my sister, my spouse; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends! Drink, yes, drink deeply, O beloved ones!

NKJV.3: I have taken off my robe; How can I put it on again? I have washed my feet; How can I defile them?
NKJV.4: My beloved put his hand By the latch of the door, And my heart yearned for him.
NKJV.5: I arose to open for my beloved, And my hands dripped with myrrh, My fingers with liquid myrrh, On the handles of the lock.

NKJV.8: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, That you tell him I am lovesick!
NKJV.9: What is your beloved More than another beloved, O fairest among women? What is your beloved More than another beloved, That you so charge us?
NKJV.10: My beloved is white and ruddy, Chief among ten thousand.
NKJV.11: His head is like the finest gold; His locks are wavy, And black as a raven.

NKJV.16: His mouth is most sweet, Yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, And this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem!

NLT.1:
I have entered my garden, my treasure, my bride!
I gather myrrh with my spices
and eat honeycomb with my honey.
I drink wine with my milk. Young Women of Jerusalem
Oh, lover and beloved, eat and drink!
Yes, drink deeply of your love!
NLT.2:
I slept, but my heart was awake,
when I heard my lover knocking and calling:
“Open to me, my treasure, my darling,
my dove, my perfect one.
My head is drenched with dew,
my hair with the dampness of the night.”
NLT.3:
But I responded,
“I have taken off my robe.
Should I get dressed again?
I have washed my feet.
Should I get them soiled?”
NLT.4:
My lover tried to unlatch the door,
and my heart thrilled within me.
NLT.5:
I jumped up to open the door for my love,
and my hands dripped with perfume.
My fingers dripped with lovely myrrh
as I pulled back the bolt.
NLT.6:
I opened to my lover,
but he was gone!
My heart sank.
I searched for him
but could not find him anywhere.
I called to him,
but there was no reply.
NLT.7:
The night watchmen found me
as they made their rounds.
They beat and bruised me
and stripped off my veil,
those watchmen on the walls.
NLT.8:
Make this promise, O women of Jerusalem —
If you find my lover,
tell him I am weak with love.
NLT.9:
Why is your lover better than all others,
O woman of rare beauty?
What makes your lover so special
that we must promise this?
NLT.10:
My lover is dark and dazzling,
better than ten thousand others!
NLT.11:
His head is finest gold,
his wavy hair is black as a raven.
NLT.12:
His eyes sparkle like doves
beside springs of water;
they are set like jewels
washed in milk.
NLT.13:
His cheeks are like gardens of spices
giving off fragrance.
His lips are like lilies,
perfumed with myrrh.
NLT.14:
His arms are like rounded bars of gold,
set with beryl.
His body is like bright ivory,
glowing with lapis lazuli.
NLT.15:
His legs are like marble pillars
set in sockets of finest gold.
His posture is stately,
like the noble cedars of Lebanon.
NLT.16:
His mouth is sweetness itself;
he is desirable in every way.
Such, O women of Jerusalem,
is my lover, my friend.

WEB.1: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.
WEB.2: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”
WEB.3: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?
WEB.4: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.
WEB.5: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
WEB.6: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left; and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.
WEB.7: The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.
WEB.8: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love.
WEB.9: How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?
WEB.10: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
WEB.11: His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.
WEB.12: His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.
WEB.13: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
WEB.14: His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.
WEB.15: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
WEB.16: His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.

AMP.1:
(The Bridegroom) "I have come into my garden, my sister, my [promised] bride;
I have gathered my myrrh along with my balsam and spice [from your sweet words].
I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey;
I have drunk my wine with my milk.
Eat, friends;
Drink and drink deeply, O lovers."
AMP.2:
(The Shulammite Bride) "I was asleep, but my heart was awake.
A voice [in my dream]! My beloved was knocking:
'Open to me, my sister, my darling,
My dove, my perfect one!
For my head is drenched with the [heavy night] dew;
My hair [is covered] with the dampness of the night.'
AMP.3:
"I had taken off my dress,
How can I put it on again?
I had washed my feet,
How could I get them dirty again?
AMP.4:
"My beloved extended his hand through the opening [of the door],
And my feelings were aroused for him.
AMP.5:
"I arose to open for my beloved;
And my hands dripped with myrrh,
And my fingers with liquid [sweet-scented] myrrh,
On the handles of the bolt.
AMP.6:
"I opened for my beloved,
But my beloved had turned away and was gone.
My heart went out to him when he spoke.
I searched for him, but I could not find him;
I called him, but he did not answer me.
AMP.7:
"The watchmen who make the rounds in the city found me.
They struck me, they wounded me;
The guardsmen of the walls took my shawl from me.
AMP.8:
"I command that you take an oath, O daughters of Jerusalem,
If you find my beloved,
As to what you tell him—
[Say that] I am sick from love [sick from being without him]."
AMP.9:
(The Chorus) "What is your beloved more than another beloved,
O most beautiful among women?
What is your beloved more than another beloved,
That you should so command us to take an oath?"
AMP.10:
(The Shulammite Bride) "My beloved is exquisitely handsome and ruddy,
Outstanding among ten thousand.
AMP.11:
"His head is like [precious] gold, pure gold;
His hair is [curly] like clusters of dates
And black as a raven.
AMP.12:
"His eyes are like doves
Beside streams of water,
Bathed in milk
And reposed in their setting.
AMP.13:
"His cheeks are like a bed of balsam,
Banks of sweet, fragrant herbs.
His lips are lilies
Dripping sweet-scented myrrh.
AMP.14:
"His hands are rods of gold
Set with beryl;
His abdomen is a figure of carved ivory
Inlaid with sapphires.
AMP.15:
"His legs are [strong and steady] pillars of alabaster
Set upon pedestals of fine gold.
His appearance is like Lebanon,
Stately and choice as the cedars.
AMP.16:
"His mouth is full of sweetness;
Yes, he is altogether lovely and desirable.
This is my beloved and this is my friend,
O daughters of Jerusalem."

MSG.1:
I went to my garden, dear friend, best lover!
breathed the sweet fragrance.
I ate the fruit and honey,
I drank the nectar and wine.
Celebrate with me, friends!
Raise your glasses—"To life! To love!"
MSG.2:
I was sound asleep, but in my dreams I was wide awake.
Oh, listen! It's the sound of my lover knocking, calling!
"Let me in, dear companion, dearest friend,
my dove, consummate lover!
I'm soaked with the dampness of the night,
drenched with dew, shivering and cold."
MSG.3:
"But I'm in my nightgown—do you expect me to get dressed?
I'm bathed and in bed—do you want me to get dirty?"
MSG.4:
But my lover wouldn't take no for an answer,
and the longer he knocked, the more excited I became.
MSG.5:
I got up to open the door to my lover,
sweetly ready to receive him,
Desiring and expectant
as I turned the door handle.
MSG.6:
But when I opened the door he was gone.
My loved one had tired of waiting and left.
And I died inside—oh, I felt so bad!
I ran out looking for him
But he was nowhere to be found.
I called into the darkness—but no answer.
MSG.7:
The night watchmen found me
as they patrolled the streets of the city.
They slapped and beat and bruised me,
ripping off my clothes,
These watchmen,
who were supposed to be guarding the city.
MSG.8:
I beg you, sisters in Jerusalem—
if you find my lover,
Please tell him I want him,
that I'm heartsick with love for him.
MSG.9:
What's so great about your lover, fair lady?
What's so special about him that you beg for our help?
MSG.10:
My dear lover glows with health—
red-blooded, radiant!
He's one in a million.
There's no one quite like him!
MSG.11:
My golden one, pure and untarnished,
with raven black curls tumbling across his shoulders.
MSG.12:
His eyes are like doves, soft and bright,
but deep-set, brimming with meaning, like wells of water.
MSG.13:
His face is rugged, his beard smells like sage,
His voice, his words, warm and reassuring.
MSG.14:
Fine muscles ripple beneath his skin,
quiet and beautiful.
His torso is the work of a sculptor,
hard and smooth as ivory.
MSG.15:
He stands tall, like a cedar,
strong and deep-rooted,
A rugged mountain of a man,
aromatic with wood and stone.
MSG.16:
His words are kisses, his kisses words.
Everything about him delights me, thrills me
through and through!
That's my lover, that's my man,
dear Jerusalem sisters.

NIV.1:
Lover
I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride;
I have gathered my myrrh with my spice.
I have eaten my honeycomb and my honey;
I have drunk my wine and my milk.
Friends
Eat, O friends, and drink;
drink your fill, O lovers.
NIV.2:
Beloved
I slept but my heart was awake.
Listen! My lover is knocking:
“Open to me, my sister, my darling,
my dove, my flawless one.
My head is drenched with dew,
my hair with the dampness of the night.”
NIV.3:
I have taken off my robe—
must I put it on again?
I have washed my feet—
must I soil them again?
NIV.4:
My lover thrust his hand through the latch-opening;
my heart began to pound for him.
NIV.5:
I arose to open for my lover,
and my hands dripped with myrrh,
my fingers with flowing myrrh,
on the handles of the lock.
NIV.6:
I opened for my lover,
but my lover had left; he was gone.
My heart sank at his departure.
I looked for him but did not find him.
I called him but he did not answer.
NIV.7:
The watchmen found me
as they made their rounds in the city.
They beat me, they bruised me;
they took away my cloak,
those watchmen of the walls!
NIV.8:
O daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you—
if you find my lover,
what will you tell him?
Tell him I am faint with love.
NIV.9:
Friends
How is your beloved better than others,
most beautiful of women?
How is your beloved better than others,
that you charge us so?
NIV.10:
Beloved
My lover is radiant and ruddy,
outstanding among ten thousand.
NIV.11:
His head is purest gold;
his hair is wavy
and black as a raven.
NIV.12:
His eyes are like doves
by the water streams,
washed in milk,
mounted like jewels.
NIV.13:
His cheeks are like beds of spice
yielding perfume.
His lips are like lilies
dripping with myrrh.
NIV.14:
His arms are rods of gold
set with chrysolite.
His body is like polished ivory
decorated with sapphires.
NIV.15:
His legs are pillars of marble
set on bases of pure gold.
His appearance is like Lebanon,
choice as its cedars.
NIV.16:
His mouth is sweetness itself;
he is altogether lovely.
This is my lover, this my friend,
O daughters of Jerusalem.

NET.1: I have entered my garden, O my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my balsam spice. I have eaten my honeycomb and my honey; I have drunk my wine and my milk! Eat, friends, and drink! Drink freely, O lovers!
NET.2: I was asleep, but my mind was dreaming. Listen! My lover is knocking at the door! “Open for me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one! My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”
NET.3: “I have already taken off my robe — must I put it on again? I have already washed my feet — must I soil them again?”
NET.4: My lover thrust his hand through the hole, and my feelings were stirred for him.
NET.5: I arose to open for my beloved; my hands dripped with myrrh — my fingers flowed with myrrh on the handles of the lock.
NET.6: I opened for my beloved, but my lover had already turned and gone away. I fell into despair when he departed. I looked for him but did not find him; I called him but he did not answer me.
NET.7: The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. They beat me, they bruised me; they took away my cloak, those watchmen on the walls!
NET.8: O maidens of Jerusalem, I command you — If you find my beloved, what will you tell him? Tell him that I am lovesick!
NET.9: Why is your beloved better than others, O most beautiful of women? Why is your beloved better than others, that you would command us in this manner?
NET.10: My beloved is dazzling and ruddy; he stands out in comparison to all other men.
NET.11: His head is like the most pure gold. His hair is curly — black like a raven.
NET.12: His eyes are like doves by streams of water, washed in milk, mounted like jewels.
NET.13: His cheeks are like garden beds full of balsam trees yielding perfume. His lips are like lilies dripping with drops of myrrh.
NET.14: His arms are like rods of gold set with chrysolite. His abdomen is like polished ivory inlaid with sapphires.
NET.15: His legs are like pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as its cedars.
NET.16: His mouth is very sweet; he is totally desirable. This is my beloved! This is my companion, O maidens of Jerusalem!
